title: Priyanka Chopra Jonas Nominated for Critics Choice Super Award for The Bluff, Adding to Breakout Awards Season
excerpt: The Indian actress competes for Best Actress in an Action Movie alongside Pamela Anderson and Charlize Theron, following her recent Emmy nomination for Heads of State.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Priyanka Chopra Jonas is nominated for Best Actress in an Action Movie at the Critics Choice Super Awards.
  • She competes against established stars like Pamela Anderson and Charlize Theron in a competitive field.
  • This nomination follows her Emmy nod for Heads of State, marking a strong awards season.
  • Winners will be announced on August 6, with Superman leading all film nominations with six nods.
  • Chopra Jonas's career reflects a growing presence of Indian talent in Hollywood.
  • Priyanka Chopra Jonas is nominated for Best Actress in an Action Movie at the 6th Critics Choice Super Awards for her role in the Amazon Prime Video film The Bluff.
  • She competes against Pamela Anderson (The Naked Gun), Charlize Theron (Apex), Eiza González, Samara Weaving, and Maddie Ziegler — a field dominated by established action stars.
  • The nomination follows her Emmy nod for Heads of State, making this her strongest awards season since transitioning to Hollywood.
  • Winners will be announced on August 6, with Superman leading all film nominations with six nods.

A Career Milestone

Priyanka Chopra Jonas has earned a nomination for Best Actress in an Action Movie at the 2026 Critics Choice Super Awards for her performance in The Bluff, the Amazon Prime Video period action-thriller directed by Frank E. Flowers. The recognition marks a significant milestone in an awards season that has increasingly validated her transition from Bollywood superstar to credible Hollywood leading lady.

The Critics Choice Super Awards, now in their sixth year, honor popular genre films and series across action, superhero, horror, and science fiction categories. Chopra Jonas will compete against a formidable field: Pamela Anderson for The Naked Gun, Charlize Theron for Apex, Eiza González for Mike & Nick & Nick & Alice, Samara Weaving for Over Your Dead Body, Akari Takaishi for Ghost Killer, and Maddie Ziegler for Pretty Lethal.

Building Momentum

The nomination arrives on the heels of Chopra Jonas's recent Emmy nomination for her role in the political thriller Heads of State, making this her most acclaimed year in Hollywood. Her previous Critics Choice Super Award nomination came in 2024 for the Amazon series Citadel, where she played spy agent Nadia Sinh — a role that demonstrated her action credentials but divided critics on the show itself.

The Bluff appears to have changed the conversation. Set in the 19th-century Caribbean, the film casts Chopra Jonas as a former pirate confronting her past to protect her family. The role required extensive physical preparation and stunt work, putting her in a category of action performance that Hollywood has historically reserved for a small cohort of actresses.

"This recognition comes hot on the heels of her recent Emmy nod for Heads of State, further affirming her growing global stature."

— Devdiscourse

The Broader Landscape

Superman leads all film nominations at the 6th Critics Choice Super Awards with six nods, while Prime Video's The Boys is the top television nominee with five. Other major film contenders include Masters of the Universe, The Fantastic Four: First Steps, and Project Hail Mary. In television, House of the Dragon and Star Trek: Strange New Worlds dominate nominations alongside The Boys.

The awards ceremony, which will announce winners on August 6, has grown into a significant marker of genre film credibility. For Chopra Jonas, a win would place her alongside previous action actress honorees who have gone on to expanded franchise opportunities and dramatic crossover roles.

An Indian Star in Hollywood's Awards Conversation

Chopra Jonas's trajectory reflects a broader opening for Indian talent in Western entertainment. She remains the most prominent Indian actress working in Hollywood, having built a career that spans Miss World 2000, five Filmfare Awards, a Padma Shri, and now serious Hollywood awards contention.

Her approach has been deliberate: after breaking into the American market with the television series Quantico in 2015, she systematically pursued roles that showcased range — romantic comedies (Isn't It Romantic), prestige drama (The White Tiger), action franchises (Citadel, The Bluff), and ensemble pieces (The Matrix Resurrections). The strategy appears to be paying off with industry recognition that earlier eluded her despite commercial success.

Also notable this awards season is fellow Indian-origin actor Himesh Patel, who earned widespread critical praise for his performance in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey — the latest in a growing list of Indian-origin performers finding substantial roles in major Western productions.

Winners across all categories will be revealed when the Critics Choice Super Awards ceremony airs on August 6.
